items.stem: What does a SignalR hub provide?

options.text: A pipeline for the server and clients to call methods on each other
options.rationale: Correct: hubs enable bidirectional RPC between server and clients.

options.text: A relational database for chat messages
options.rationale: A hub is not a database.
A hub is an application construct, not a transport-security layer.
Hubs handle real-time messaging, not static files.

items.explanation: Correct: hubs enable bidirectional RPC between server and clients.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO statements about SignalR transports are correct? (Select TWO.)

options.text: WebSockets is the preferred transport when available
options.rationale: Correct: WebSockets generally gives the best performance.

options.text: SignalR automatically falls back to other transports when WebSockets is unavailable
options.rationale: Correct: it falls back to SSE or long polling.

options.text: SignalR only works over WebSockets and fails otherwise
options.rationale: It falls back to other transports.

options.text: Long polling is always faster than WebSockets

items.explanation: Correct: WebSockets is preferred, with automatic fallback to other transports.

items.stem: To push an update only to agents handling a given queue, which SignalR feature fits best?

options.rationale: Correct: groups let the server target a subset of connections.
Creating hubs per message is unnecessary and wrong.
Closing connections does not target a subset.

items.explanation: Correct: groups let the server target a subset of connections.
